profile.summary: This is one paper's evaluation, not a released suite. For each gene knocked down or activated in a CRISPR screen, every other gene is scored by its link to the perturbed gene, either an attention weight taken from a single-cell foundation model or a Spearman correlation, and the score is used to classify which genes turn out to be differentially expressed. Performance is the per-perturbation area under the ROC curve. The same test is run for three univariate gene-level features, variance, mean expression and dropout rate, and then a conditional test asks whether adding a pairwise edge score to those gene-level features improves prediction. The answer the paper reports is no: gene-level features reach 0.81 to 0.88 against about 0.70 for either edge type, and adding edges changes the area under the curve by about nothing. The evaluation is useful as a sanity check that anyone claiming regulatory signal in attention has to pass.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Results, Perturbation-first validation and No incremental pairwise value sections; Methods, Perturbation-first validation and Confound decomposition

summary_quotes.text: For each CRISPRi perturbation, we computed edge scores between the perturbed gene and all other genes, then evaluated AUROC for classifying differentially expressed targets.

Critically, trivial gene-level baselines—variance, mean expression, and dropout rate—all outperform both attention and correlation edges on Objective B (AUROC 0.81–0.88 vs. 0.70; all $$p < 10^{-12}$$ ; Fig. 3).
Gene-level features alone achieve AUROC $$= 0.895$$ [bootstrap 95% CI: 0.884, 0.905]; adding attention yields $$\Delta$$ AUROC $$= -0.0004$$

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: The paper calls this Objective B, and keeps it apart from Objective A, which is recovery of curated regulatory interactions. Objective B asks whether a pairwise score between a perturbed gene and another gene predicts that the other gene will be differentially expressed after the perturbation. The author stresses that this is an effect-magnitude question, mixing direct regulation, indirect propagation and how detectable a gene is at all, so the two objectives can disagree: a true direct edge may produce little differential expression, and a non-regulatory feature can score well if it proxies target susceptibility. The evaluation therefore sets a floor rather than a ceiling, that any claimed pairwise regulatory signal must first beat features computed from single genes.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Evaluation framework section; Results, Perturbation-first validation

quotes.text: Objective B (perturbation-response prediction). Do attention-derived edge scores predict which genes will show differential expression after a CRISPRi or CRISPRa perturbation of a source gene? This is an effect- magnitude task that integrates direct regulation, indirect propagation, and target susceptibility.
an edge can be a genuine direct regulatory link yet contribute little to Objective B
any claimed pairwise regulatory signal must first exceed gene-level features on this task

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The expression data are published CRISPR screens, taken through the scperturb package according to the code repository: the Replogle genome-scale CRISPRi screens in K562, described in the paper as more than 640,000 K562 cells and 2,024 perturbed genes, and in RPE1, Adamson CRISPRa in K562 with 77 perturbations, Tian iPSC neurons with 7, and Shifrut primary T cells with 7. Tabula Sapiens tissues and a brain data set are used for the other objective. Preprocessing is standard Scanpy quality control, genes in at least 3 cells, cells with at least 200 genes, normalisation to 10,000 counts and a log transform, with highly variable gene selection. Labels come from the screens themselves: for each perturbation, a Mann-Whitney test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and a log fold change threshold marks which genes are differentially expressed. The pairwise scores being tested are attention weights from Geneformer V2-316M, averaged over heads within a layer and then over cells, and Spearman correlation edges computed from the same control cells, with absolute value taken because the sign is not comparable. The evaluation universe is 2,000 highly variable genes for K562 and 3,309 for RPE1, where the perturbed genes are forced into the set.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Two layers of test. The first is per-perturbation area under the ROC curve: rank all candidate genes for one perturbation by the score under test and ask how well that ranking separates the differentially expressed genes, then compare score types across perturbations with paired tests. On K562 CRISPRi, correlation edges reach 0.696 under the primary settings with 151 perturbations, and all 27 sensitivity conditions give 0.62 to 0.76; Geneformer attention at layer 13 reaches 0.704 on 280 evaluable perturbations, indistinguishable from correlation at 0.703. Variance alone reaches 0.881. The second test is conditional: a data set of 280 by 1,999 perturbation and gene observations, 559,720 pairs with a 2.8 per cent positive rate, five logistic regression models under 5-fold GroupKFold cross validation grouped by perturbation. Gene-level features alone reach 0.895, adding attention changes the area under the curve by minus 0.0004 and adding correlation by minus 0.002. Harder splits were also tried, GroupKFold by target gene and joint gene by perturbation splits, with gradient boosted trees as well as logistic regression and with AUPRC and top-k recall as well as AUROC. Propensity matching, five differential-expression-negative targets matched to each positive one on mean, variance and dropout rate, gives 59,153 matched pairs in which attention retains 0.609 raw discriminability but zero incremental value. All tests use Benjamini-Hochberg correction at 0.05, and bootstrap intervals resample at the perturbation level. A synthetic positive control with a planted network shows the same pipeline detects a real pairwise signal, reporting a change in area under the curve of plus 0.518 in the cleanest variant.

Variance alone achieves AUROC $$= 0.881$$

We constructed a dataset of $$280 \times 1{,}999$$ perturbation–gene observations (559,720 pairs, 2.8% positive rate) and compared five logistic-regression models under 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation: gene-level features only (mean expression, variance, dropout rate), attention edge only, correlation edge only, gene-level plus attention, and gene-level plus correlation.

we tested progressively harder generalisation protocols—cross-gene splits (GroupKFold by target gene, preventing gene-level propensity leakage), joint cross-gene $$\times$$ cross-perturbation splits—and both linear (logistic regression) and nonlinear (GBDT) models across AUROC, AUPRC, and top- k recall.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The analysis code is published as a repository, archived on Zenodo. Create the conda environment from the file in src, let the scperturb package download the perturbation data, and run the module scripts: one for the perturbation-first validation and the trivial baselines, another for the RPE1 confound battery. The repository says each module is self-contained, loads data from external sources or precomputed checkpoints in results, and writes outputs back into results, with resume support. Geneformer weights come from Hugging Face. The licence statement asks anyone wanting to reuse the repository to contact the author first.

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Cross validation over perturbations, not a fixed train and test release. The main incremental-value test uses 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by perturbation, so a perturbation's pairs sit entirely in one fold. Harder protocols group by target gene, to stop a gene's own propensity leaking between folds, and combine both into a joint cross-gene by cross-perturbation split. A nested cross-validation protocol is used when choosing the best Geneformer layer out of 18. The primary evaluation layer, layer 13, was fixed in advance from a separate brain data set before any K562 perturbation data were examined.

The primary attention layer (L13) was pre-specified based on independent DLPFC brain data

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Per-perturbation AUROC for classifying differentially expressed genes, higher is better, is the primary measure. The conditional test reports the change in AUROC from adding an edge score to the gene-level model, with bootstrap confidence intervals, and the harder protocols also report AUPRC and top-k recall. Paired comparisons use Wilcoxon tests and Cohen's d.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Several, and they are the point of the design. Cross validation is grouped by perturbation, and in the harder protocols by target gene, so a gene's own susceptibility cannot leak across folds. Propensity matching pairs each differentially expressed target with five non-targets of similar mean, variance and dropout rate, which removes the gene-level advantage before the edge score is judged. Cross-fitted residualisation removes expression covariates from the edge scores. The primary layer was chosen on an independent data set before the perturbation data were seen. There is no control for the perturbation data having been in the foundation models' pretraining corpora.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Confound decomposition; Results, No incremental pairwise value

quotes.text: Hard-generalisation protocols use GroupKFold by target gene and joint cross-gene $$\times$$ cross-perturbation splits. Cross-fitted residualisation removes expression-covariate contributions from edge scores using 5-fold OLS and GBDT
Propensity-score matching uses logistic regression on gene-level features to match each DE-positive target to $$k = 5$$ DE-negative targets with similar covariate profiles
The primary attention layer (L13) was pre-specified based on independent DLPFC brain data

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Bootstrap confidence intervals with 200 iterations, resampled at the perturbation level unless stated otherwise, reported for the changes in AUROC. Paired p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg correction at 0.05 across a declared family of 95 confirmatory tests out of 153 in all. A power statement is given for the main null: 559,720 observations give more than 99 per cent power to detect a change in AUROC of 0.005.

quotes.text: Bootstrap confidence intervals use 200 iterations with perturbation-level resampling unless otherwise noted.

facts.value: Control cell expression, and a model's internals. facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Zero-shot for the foundation models, with a small supervised classifier on top of the features. The published checkpoints are read as they are, Geneformer V2-316M and V1-10M and the scGPT whole-human checkpoint, with no fine-tuning; what is fitted is the logistic regression or gradient boosted model that combines gene-level features and edge scores under cross validation.

quotes.text: We use Geneformer V1-10M (6 layers, 4 heads) for multi-model comparison and Geneformer V2-316M (18 layers, 18 heads) as the primary model for all layer-level mechanistic analyses
Gene-level features (mean expression, variance, dropout rate) and pairwise edge scores are used in logistic regression under 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation (grouped by perturbation).

strengths.text: It makes the baseline do the work. Three features computable from the expression matrix alone, variance, mean and dropout rate, are run through the same pipeline, and they beat both edge types, which turns a vague claim about attention into a measurable comparison.

quotes.text: Critically, trivial gene-level baselines—variance, mean expression, and dropout rate—all outperform both attention and correlation edges on Objective B (AUROC 0.81–0.88 vs. 0.70; all $$p < 10^{-12}$$ ; Fig. 3).
any claimed pairwise regulatory signal must first exceed gene-level features on this task

strengths.text: The null result is backed by a sensitivity check of the pipeline itself. On synthetic data with a planted network, and with expression z-scored so univariate variance carries no information about the truth, the same incremental-value test finds a change in AUROC of plus 0.518, and a shuffled control gives nearly zero.

quotes.text: Under planted ground truth, the full incremental-value pipeline detects pairwise signal cleanly: $$\Delta$$ AUROC of $$+0.518$$
Per-gene expression was z-scored post-hoc so univariate variance is uninformative about ground-truth target status, isolating pairwise signal from univariate baselines.

strengths.text: The confounds are attacked from more than one side: grouped cross validation, harder cross-gene and joint splits, linear and nonlinear models, three metrics, residualisation of expression covariates and propensity matching, and the conclusion is the same each time.

strengths.text: The choice that could most easily have been fitted to the result was fixed in advance: layer 13 was pre-specified from an independent brain data set before any K562 perturbation data were examined, and the 18-layer profile is reported as a planned secondary analysis.

K562 uses 2,000 highly variable genes and RPE1 3,309 with the perturbed genes forced in, and the paper shows that restricting RPE1 to 2,000 genes changes the attention advantage by plus 0.168, so scores are not comparable across these settings.

limitations.text: The endpoint is not regulation.
